clauses.text: A claim line is a duplicate when the member, the billing provider, the date of service, the procedure code, the modifiers and the units all match a line the plan has already processed.
When the earlier line was paid, the duplicate denial is correct and no further action is needed. The provider should not resubmit or appeal.

A service that was in fact performed more than once on the same day is not a duplicate. The repeat line must carry modifier 76 (same clinician) or 77 (different clinician), and the record must document each performance separately, with times or distinct findings.

A change to a claim that has already been processed must be sent as a replacement claim that references the original claim number. A changed claim sent as a new claim is denied as a duplicate; the provider should resubmit it as a replacement.
When the earlier line was itself denied, the duplicate denial does not decide the matter. The provider should act on the reason for the earlier denial.
